passage: I'm Tejas, and my little brother Samir is two. In the kitchen he reached up for the stove knob. Papa said, "No, Samir. Hot." Samir stopped, looked at Papa's face, and pulled his hand back, pouting. Then he toddled over and hugged Papa's knees. When Dadaji came in from his walk, Samir ran to him, patted his feet and climbed into his lap. I don't know how much he understands, but he listens to them.

qa.q: What did Samir reach for in the kitchen?
qa.a: He reached up for the stove knob.

qa.q: What does Samir's pout suggest when he pulled his hand back?
qa.a: It suggests he felt a little disappointed at being stopped, but he still chose to accept Papa's guidance.

qa.q: How could Papa help Samir keep accepting safety limits?
qa.a: He could keep using short, calm words like "Hot" and gently steer Samir to something he is allowed to touch.

qa.q: How might Dadaji feel when Samir runs to him and pats his feet?
qa.a: He would likely feel loved and happy to be greeted so warmly by his grandson.

grounding: Shows a toddler accepting a parent's guidance and showing natural affection for an elder, seen by his brother.

passage:
Saturday: At the busy market, Vijay slipped out of Avni's hand and ran toward the road. She caught him. "Stop! We hold hands here." He screamed and kicked.
Wednesday: At the colony gate, Vijay paused, looked back at Avni and held up his hand.
The next Saturday: He waited at the kerb, holding her fingers, then spotted his Nani outside the sweet shop and tugged Avni over so he could hug Nani's legs.

qa.q: What did Vijay do at the colony gate on Wednesday?
qa.a: He paused, looked back at Avni and held up his hand.

qa.q: What does Vijay looking back at Avni at the gate suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he remembered her rule and was checking with her; he seemed calmer and more accepting than when he screamed and kicked at the market.

qa.q: What helped Vijay learn to hold hands near roads?
qa.a: Avni used the same short rule each time and kept to it calmly, even when he screamed, so it became familiar.

qa.q: How might Nani feel when Vijay tugs Avni over to hug her legs?
qa.a: She would likely feel warm and delighted that her grandson wanted to reach her so eagerly. ❤️

grounding: Shows a toddler coming to accept a parent's authority over several days and showing affection to an elder.

passage: In a housing society garden in Delhi, Amandeep flung a handful of sand into the air. Minakshi knelt in front of him. "Sand stays down, puttar." He frowned, looked at her face, then slowly opened his fist and let the sand fall. A moment later his Biji came along the path with her walking stick. Amandeep dropped his spade, toddled to her, patted her knee and held the spade up for her to see.

qa.q: What did Amandeep fling into the air?
qa.a: He flung a handful of sand into the air.

qa.q: What was Amandeep thinking when he frowned and looked at Minakshi's face?
qa.a: He seemed to be weighing whether to keep playing his way, and her calm face helped him decide to follow what she said.

qa.q: What made Minakshi's guidance easy for Amandeep to follow?
qa.a: She got down to his level and gave one short, clear rule instead of shouting from a distance.

qa.q: How might Biji see Amandeep toddling to her with his spade?
qa.a: She would probably feel loved and pleased that he wanted to share his play with her.

grounding: Illustrates a toddler deferring to his mother's guidance and showing warm affection for his grandmother.

passage:
"Trisha, hot! Don't touch." Damini lifted her hand from near the stove.
Trisha's lip wobbled. "Hot?"
"Yes, hot. Ouch. Come play here."
Trisha looked at the flame, then at her mother, and toddled to her pots on the floor.
"Good listening."
When Nani came in with her cane, Trisha dropped the pot and hugged Nani's legs.
"Arre, my little one!"
"Nani sit," Trisha said, pulling her to the chair.

qa.q: Where did Damini lead Trisha to play?
qa.a: She led her to play with her pots on the floor.

qa.q: What does Trisha looking at the flame, then at her mother, suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she was unsure but trusted her mother's warning enough to follow it.

qa.q: How could Damini keep encouraging Trisha to accept guidance?
qa.a: She can keep warnings short and clear, give a safe alternative, and praise her for listening, as she did here.

qa.q: How might Nani feel when Trisha hugs her legs and pulls her to the chair?
qa.a: She would probably feel loved and cared for by her granddaughter. ❤️

grounding: Illustrates a toddler accepting a parent's guidance and showing natural affection towards an elder.

passage:
Home-to-daycare diary, from Karthik's father, Pradeep
On Sunday we visited Thatha. When Thatha said, 'Karthik, shoes off inside,' Karthik stopped and pulled at his sandals right away, though at home he fights us about it. He sat close to Thatha all evening and kept patting his knee. At dinner, when I said 'enough sweets,' he pouted but put the laddu down. We were pleasantly surprised.

qa.q: Whom did the family visit on Sunday?
qa.a: They visited Thatha.

qa.q: What might Karthik have felt towards Thatha, based on his behaviour?
qa.a: He seems to feel both respect and warmth for Thatha, since he obeyed him quickly and stayed close, patting his knee.

qa.q: What could the daycare teacher take from this note?
qa.a: She could see that Karthik listens well to calm, trusted adults, and use short, friendly instructions with him.

qa.q: Why might Thatha's words work better than the parents' at home?
qa.a: Karthik may see Thatha as a special elder and be eager to please him, while at home he is testing limits with his parents.

grounding: Shows a toddler deferring to parental and grandparental guidance and showing affection for an elder, in a father's diary note.
